n: These are teachings Joseph gave on April 2, 1843, at Ramus, Illinois. First: when Christ appears, we’ll see him as he truly is—a glorified man, like us in form.

f.w: we shall see him as he is

n: The friendships and social bonds we enjoy here will continue in heaven, but with eternal glory added.
Joseph corrects a common belief: John 14:23 describes a real, personal visit of the Father and Son, not just a feeling in the heart.

f.g: Belonging to a sect or denomination; here, traditional Christian teaching of the time.

n: A question: is time measured differently for God, angels, prophets, and humans according to where they live?
Yes. And only angels who belong or have belonged to this earth minister to it.

f.w: angels who minister to this earth

n: Angels don’t live on a planet like ours.
They live in God’s presence, on a globe like a sea of glass and fire, where past, present, and future are all visible.

f.w: a sea of glass and fire

n: God’s dwelling place is itself a great Urim and Thummim—a means of seeing and knowing all things.

f.g: Hebrew, often understood as “lights and perfections”; sacred instruments for receiving revelation.

n: The earth itself will become like crystal, a Urim and Thummim for its celestial inhabitants, revealing lower kingdoms. It will belong to Christ.

f.w: This earth, in its sanctified and immortal state

n: The “white stone” in Revelation 2:17 will become a personal Urim and Thummim for each who receives one, revealing higher kingdoms.

f.w: the white stone mentioned in Revelation 2:17

n: Each who enters the celestial kingdom receives a white stone with a new name only he knows—the “key word.”
Joseph prophesies that bloodshed before Christ’s coming will begin in South Carolina—fulfilled when the Civil War began there in 1861.
It would likely arise over slavery. Joseph says he received this on December 25, 1832—the same date as D&C 87.

f.g: The controversy over slavery, a central cause of the American Civil War.

n: Joseph once prayed earnestly to know when Christ would come, and heard a voice.

f.w: the time of the coming of the Son of Man

n: The voice: if Joseph lived to 85, he would see Christ’s face—so stop asking. Joseph would have turned 85 in December 1890.

f.w: let this suffice, and trouble me no more
f.g: Suffice = be enough. God sometimes withholds exact timing.

n: Joseph couldn’t tell whether this meant the Millennium, some earlier appearance, or seeing Christ after his own death. He honestly admits his uncertainty.

f.g: He was left with an ambiguous answer.

n: His conclusion: Christ will not come before that time.

f.w: will not be any sooner than that time

n: A beloved teaching: whatever intelligence we gain in this life rises with us in the resurrection. Learning has eternal value.
Someone who gains more knowledge through diligence and obedience will have that advantage in the next life.

f.g: Both effort and righteous living are named; knowledge here is more than information.

n: There is an unchangeable law, decreed before the world, on which every blessing depends.

f.g: Unable to be reversed or cancelled.

n: When we receive any blessing, it is through obeying the law it depends on.
A defining doctrine: the Father and Son have tangible bodies of flesh and bones; the Holy Ghost is a spirit, which is why he can dwell within us.

f.w: The Father has a body of flesh and bones

n: A person may receive the Holy Ghost’s influence briefly without it remaining with him; keeping it requires worthiness.
